content.text:
I've submitted the campaign, but none of the three compositions I measured produced a real photocurrent. I submitted index 16 (Mg 0.32 / Mn 0.68) as the best.

The library had only 3 photocurrent measurements, so I spread them across the Mg–Mn composition line:

| Index | Mg fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.08 | −0.0 |
| 16 | 0.32 | −0.0 |
| 24 | 0.71 | −1e-8 |

Index 16 is tied with index 3 for the highest reading, which is effectively zero. I picked it over index 3 because it sits at the composition of the MgMn₂O₄ spinel. Under the 3.22 eV illumination, the Mg–Mn oxide system looks essentially inactive across the range I sampled.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements before the photocurrent budget ran out. Large gaps between the measured points were never tested, including the Mg 0.4–0.6 and above-0.75 regions. So a more active composition could still be in the library.
